💬 Iran will not negotiate, reopen Hormuz until its conditions are met: Security chief

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran will not enter negotiations with the United States or reopen the Strait of Hormuz until Washington meets seven conditions set by Tehran, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said on Wednesday.

Rezaei said Iran’s conditions were completely different from those of the past and that Tehran would not return to previous arrangements.
​
“Until our conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened and we will not negotiate,” Rezaei said.
​
He said Iran wanted the United States to take action first to restore the trust of the Iranian people, stressing that Washington would have to act before Tehran would consider entering negotiations.
​
Rezaei said Qatar, Pakistan and Iraq had asked Iran about its conditions and that Iran had provided written conditions to be relayed to the United States. He said Iran’s conditions were currently in the hands of Pakistan and Qatar.
​
The security chief said Iran’s decision not to negotiate until its conditions were met was based on its assessment that the United States could not be trusted. He said Iran was seeking to pursue diplomacy from a different position and would not return to the previous circumstances.
​
Rezaei also urged regional countries not to become involved in US efforts to restrict Iranian aviation. Referring to a US plan to impose sanctions on Iranian aircraft, he called on neighboring countries not to join US moves and said regional states should work to prevent the conflict from spreading.
​
“If they prevent Iranian aircraft from flying, their airports will also be unable to operate flights,” Rezaei said.
​
Rezaei also said Iran had emerged from the war in a stronger position, stressing that the country was now at the peak of its standing and that Iran today was not the same as it was before the war.
